randomize_dircolors.py.summary: Write a ``~/.ls_colors`` file with a random true-colour for every file extension.
details: Keeps a list of common extensions, picks a bright colour for each one, builds the ``LS_COLORS`` string with 24-bit codes and saves the shell snippet to ``/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.ls_colors`` for sourcing.

raster.py.summary: Rename a compiled extension to the Android CPython 3.14 file name.
details: Takes the current file and a new stem and renames the file to ``<stem>.cpython-314-arm-linux-androideabi.so`` in the same directory.

reformat_module_docstring.py.summary: Reflow the module docstrings of Python files to a fixed width.
details: Locates the module docstring with :mod:`tokenize`, rewraps its prose while keeping paragraphs and lists intact and writes the file back only when the text changed.

reinstall_system_pkgs.py.summary: Reinstall a list of apt packages one by one, logging the failures.
details: Reads the package names from the given file and runs ``apt install --reinstall -y`` for each of them, appending the packages that fail to ``~/reinstall_failed.txt``.

remove_lines_containing_str_from_files.p.summary: Delete the lines containing a string from many text files.
details: Removes every line that contains the given substring (the last argument; the preceding arguments are the files, defaulting to all non-binary files below the current directory) and reports the lines removed per file plus the space freed. Work is spread over a process pool.

rename-project.py.summary: Rename a project by replacing its old name in file names, text files and Hatch/pyproject metadata.
details: Walks the tree, replaces the old project name in the text-like files (README, license, requirements, makefiles, dotfiles, Python sources ...) and renames the matching files and directories, skipping the files that do not look textual.

rename_by_parent.py.summary: Rename every ``README.pdf`` after the directory that contains it.
details: Walks the tree with a stack-based directory walker and renames each ``README.pdf`` to ``<parent-directory-name>.pdf``, unless that name already exists.

rename_html_by_title.py.summary: Rename HTML files after the title of the page.
details: Extracts the ``<title>`` (tree-sitter when available, otherwise a regex), transliterates non-Latin titles, normalises the result into a safe file name within the length limit and renames the files below the current directory in parallel, reporting the results.

rename_svg_fonts.py.summary: Rename SVG font files after their ``<font id="...">`` attribute.
details: Reads each ``.svg`` file, extracts the font id, sanitises the characters that cannot appear in a file name and renames the file to ``<font-id>.svg``, refusing to overwrite an existing target.

render_diagram.py.summary: Wrap a Mermaid or SVG diagram in a self-contained HTML page.
details: Reads the ``.mmd``/``.svg`` file, embeds the diagram (Mermaid loaded from its CDN, or the SVG inlined as a data URI) into a minimal HTML document and writes it next to the source with an ``.html`` suffix.

renm.py.summary: Rename the non-English file names below a directory to their English translation.
details: Detects names that contain non-ASCII characters, translates the stem with ``deep_translator`` in a worker pool, resolves collisions and renames the files and directories (deepest paths first). ``--directory`` selects the root, ``--pool-method`` the multiprocessing style.

renneng.py.summary: Translate the non-English file and directory names of the current directory to English.
details: Walks the tree bottom-up, translates every name that contains non-ASCII characters with Google Translate and renames the entry, adding a numeric suffix when the translated name already exists.

replace_symlink_with_orig.py.summary: Replace symlinks with copies of the files they point to.
details: Walks the given paths, copies the target content over each symlink (preserving metadata), logs the replacements to ``replaced.txt`` and the failures to ``errors.txt``, and processes the tree in parallel.

restore_all_historical_deletions.py.summary: Restore every file that was ever deleted in the repository history.
details: Reads ``git log --diff-filter=D`` to find the deletions and the commit that removed each file, checks out the version from the parent commit, stages it and finally commits everything with the message ``removed files``.
